concepts.learning_objective: Define flow of control and recognise sequence as statements executed in the order written.
Identify selection and repetition as the two control structures supported by Python.
Explain how if and if..else statements choose between blocks based on a condition.
Trace an if..elif..else chain to find which block executes.
Explain how Python uses indentation to form blocks and predict the effect of indentation on output.

topics.title: Repetition and the for loop with range()

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a loop's control variable and condition decide repetition and termination.
Trace a for loop to count the number of iterations.
Determine the sequence generated by range() with start, stop and step values.
Trace a while loop and determine the values of variables after it ends.
Recognise an infinite loop and explain why its condition never becomes false.
Explain how break terminates a loop and predict the resulting output.
Explain how continue skips the rest of an iteration and predict the resulting output.
Define a nested loop and count how many times its inner body executes.
Trace nested loops that print number patterns and prime numbers.
